transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-19 15:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Dmitri Novak (Redwood SE), Alicia Ramos (NimbleRetail Head of ML), Tom Becker (Infra), Priya Singh (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Kickoff to scope POC benchmarks and harness integration focusing on traffic fidelity and streaming fallback behavior.
- Agreement to run a mixed-mode soak and provide customer scripts.
- Action items: share template, run 24h soak, workshop on streaming fallback policy.

Topics: benchmark success criteria; workload sizing; streaming vs non-streaming behaviour; KV-cache warmup; fallback triggers; runbook and acceptance gates.

Transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: All right, thanks for joining everyone. Uh, quick intros if we haven't all met — I'm Maya, AE on the account, and with me is Dmitri, our SE who'll be running the benchmark side.
00:12 Alicia Ramos: Hey, thanks. Alicia here, heading ML at NimbleRetail. We have Tom on infra and Priya for product. Thanks for doing this.
00:18 Tom Becker: Hi all.
00:20 Dmitri Novak: Hi. So the purpose today is to nail down what we need to run a representative benchmark and how the harness plugs into their scripts, and the streaming fallback playbook.
00:32 Priya Singh: Correct. Our main constraint is latency SLOs for shopper-facing autocomplete and a cost target for token ops; we can't blow the margin.
00:40 Maya Chen: Great. Can you summarize current stack? Alicia?
00:44 Alicia Ramos: Sure — we run inference on a blend: internal GPU servers for heavy ops and a cloud endpoint for burst. Models are quantized int8 for most, but we've got some fp16 for high-quality paths. Traffic: 70% autocomplete (short prompts, 8-40 tokens), 20% assistant-building (200-800 tokens), 10% embeddings.
01:05 Dmitri Novak: Helpful. For the POC we usually ask for a 1k-10k request sample that matches token-distribution and a few long-tail cases. The harness will replay those with configurable concurrency, pacing, and streaming vs non-streaming modes.
01:18 Alicia Ramos: We'll export a 1k representative set. One thing: our KV cache behavior is weird on cold starts; warmup is significant for tail latency.
01:26 Dmitri Novak: Yep, KV cache warmup is a big factor. We'll capture cold, warm, and steady-state windows. For streaming we measure first-byte latency and average completion latency; for non-streaming we measure end-to-end.
01:40 Tom Becker: For us, the big ops question is how Redwood's batcher interacts with our burst window. If continuous batching holds requests to get throughput, it might bump P50 but help P95 — we need to see the tradeoff.
01:55 Maya Chen: Good point. Success criteria — let's be explicit. Priya, what's an acceptable P95 for autocomplete?
02:00 Priya Singh: For autocomplete we want P95 < 120ms, ideally P50 < 40ms. For longer assistant flows, P95 < 800ms, cost per 1k tokens under our threshold — I'll share the target later.
02:12 Dmitri Novak: Noted. We'll instrument token-level cost estimates and produce a per-route dashboard.
02:18 Alicia Ramos: Does Redwood support per-route rollouts? We may want to route only 10% through streaming initially.
02:23 Maya Chen: Yes, we support traffic split and can do canary rollouts by route and model variant.
02:28 Dmitri Novak: About streaming fallback — our typical approach is: stream when the model variant supports chunked output and network conditions permit; fall back to non-streaming if tokens stall or connection errors exceed threshold. We'll propose trigger thresholds.
02:42 Tom Becker: We need deterministic behavior for retries — if streaming times out, we prefer a full non-streamed re-request rather than partial dupes at the app layer.
02:50 Dmitri Novak: Understood. We'll add idempotency keys and client adapter guidance in the runbook.
02:56 Alicia Ramos: How do we validate KV-cache hit rates? Can the harness emulate warmed caches?
03:00 Dmitri Novak: The harness can pre-run prefix requests to warm caches. We can run controlled warmup windows and measure improvements. We also capture KV hit/miss counters if the agent emits them — if not, we'll infer via latency curves.
03:13 Priya Singh: For the soak, how long should the steady-state run be? We need enough time to show tail behavior — maybe 24 hours?
03:18 Dmitri Novak: We recommend a 24-hour mixed-mode soak to capture diurnal variance and edge cases. For initial acceptance, a shorter 4-hour stress test at peak QPS is useful.
03:26 Maya Chen: Timeline: 2 business days to get scripts + sample traffic, Redwood sets up harness and baseline runs in 3 days, then we run 4h stress and then the 24h soak next week. Sound OK?
03:36 Alicia Ramos: That aligns. We can get the file to you by end of day Friday.
03:40 Tom Becker: On infra, we'll need a document describing egress and IP allowlist for the dedicated runner.
03:45 Maya Chen: We'll share the network checklist and security pack — SOC2 bits included.
03:49 Priya Singh: About success criteria gating — what exact metrics will we sign off on?
03:52 Dmitri Novak: Proposal: 1) Route-level P50/P95 vs target windows for short/long routes, 2) 24h soak no P95 regressions >20% compared to baseline, 3) cold-start tail < X ms (we'll compute baseline), 4) cost per 1k tokens within agreed budget. We'll formalize in the template.
04:12 Alicia Ramos: Sounds reasonable. Can you include quantization guidance — e.g., when to push int8 vs q4 for our workload?
04:18 Dmitri Novak: Yes, Dmitri: we'll add model variant recommendations; Redwood Optimize will propose quant profiles after seeing token distribution. For the POC we'll test two variants: q4 and int8 (or the customer's current config).
04:30 Priya Singh: Any concerns about noisy neighbors on dedicated pools? We may want reserved instances for predictable latency.
04:35 Maya Chen: For Dedicated we can carve reserved capacity; for hosted we have multi-tenant pools. We'll outline tradeoffs in the decision doc.
04:43 Tom Becker: Also, instrument tracing — if a request hits fallback, we need a clear span indicating that.
04:47 Dmitri Novak: Agreed. We'll include tracing hooks and a telemetry contract.
04:50 Alicia Ramos: A couple of gotchas — some of our long prompt flows include database calls mid-stream; streaming behavior combined with backend IO creates jitter. We need to simulate those pauses.
04:59 Dmitri Novak: We can add pause points in the harness scripts to emulate upstream IO. Please annotate where those occur in the traffic file.
05:05 Priya Singh: Ok, what's the acceptance checklist after the soak?
05:08 Maya Chen: Recap acceptance: meet per-route latency targets, cost within threshold, zero functional regressions in output quality (we'll run eval prompts), and a documented fallback runbook.
05:20 Alicia Ramos: Who's the primary contact for telemetry access?
05:22 Dmitri Novak: Dmitri will own the bench infra and share dashboard access. Maya will be funnel for procurement and security questions.
05:28 Tom Becker: Procurement note: we may need a short-term dedicated pool for the soak if capacity on our internal fleet isn't stable.
05:33 Maya Chen: We'll price a short reserved run for the POC and include in the proposal.
05:38 Priya Singh: One more thing — can Redwood's harness simulate progressive concurrency ramps? We need to ramp to peak over 20 minutes and then hold.
05:45 Dmitri Novak: Yes, the harness supports ramp profiles: linear, step, and custom. We'll provide a sample ramp file.
05:50 Maya Chen: Great. Any final questions?
05:52 Alicia Ramos: No, just to confirm we'll get the template and sample connector by Friday.
05:56 Maya Chen: Yes. Thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts and an invite for Oct 26 workshop.
06:02 Priya Singh: Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
